cases.note: Contradiction is expressed through valid/invalid paraphrase in longer context.
cases.premise: The incident report says the access token remained valid through the review window.
cases.query: The same review summary later states the access token was invalid during the review window.

cases.note: Permitted/forbidden conflict without an explicit negation marker.
cases.premise: A policy note records the export as permitted for research users.
cases.query: The compliance memo describes the same export as forbidden for research users.

cases.premise: The deployment checklist marks rollback as possible after the migration.
cases.query: The final release note says rollback is impossible after the migration.

cases.note: Same metric and condition, different numeric values.
cases.premise: The benchmark card reports median latency of 240 ms for model A under load.
cases.query: The comparison paragraph reports median latency of 410 ms for model A under the same load.

cases.note: Same quantity and raw value under incompatible units.
cases.premise: The shipping manifest lists the crate mass as 12 kg after calibration.
cases.query: The audit copy lists the crate mass as 12 lb after calibration.

cases.note: Context changed; the value and unit agree, so this is not a contradiction.
cases.premise: The shipping manifest lists the crate mass as 12 kg before calibration.
cases.query: The audit copy lists the crate mass as 12 kg after calibration.

cases.note: Query violates a definitional property without using the word false.
cases.premise: The glossary defines a triangle as a polygon with exactly three sides.
cases.query: The generated explanation says a triangle can have four sides while remaining a triangle.

cases.note: The query's own divisor list violates the prime definition.
cases.premise: The math note says a prime number has exactly two positive divisors.
cases.query: The answer claims 9 is prime because it has divisors 1, 3, and 9.

cases.note: Additional visual detail does not violate the definition.
cases.premise: The glossary defines a square as a figure with four equal sides.
cases.query: The caption describes the tile as a square with four equal sides and a blue border.

cases.note: A bypassing subclass counters the universal approval claim.
cases.premise: All production agents must pass human approval before release.
cases.query: The exception log says emergency production agents bypass human approval before release.

cases.note: Specific edited instance counters an every/immutable universal.
cases.premise: Every archived dataset is immutable after publication.
cases.query: A correction entry says archived dataset A17 was edited after publication.

cases.note: Most allows exceptions; this should not be scored as a contradiction.
cases.premise: Most archived datasets are immutable after publication.
cases.query: A correction entry says archived dataset A17 was edited after publication.

cases.note: Always-since claim conflicts with a later introduction date.
cases.premise: The vendor page says the API has always required token signing since 2018.
cases.query: The migration note says token signing was introduced in 2022.

cases.note: A broad always claim conflicts with a later dated state.
cases.premise: The runbook says the service always used manual review in 2019.
cases.query: The audit says the same service used automated review in 2021.

cases.note: A system can change across time without contradiction.
cases.premise: The service used manual review in 2019.
cases.query: The service used automated review in 2021.

cases.premise: The model declined the unsafe request and offered a safe alternative.
cases.query: The model refused the unsafe request while suggesting a safe alternative.

cases.note: Two cautious negative claims are compatible.
cases.premise: The audit found no evidence that private keys left the vault.
cases.query: The audit did not prove that private keys left the vault.
